title: Email uniqueness validation - reject duplicate email on registration
gherkin:
Feature: Unique Email Address Validation
  Scenario: System rejects duplicate email during registration
    Given a user account exists with email "user@example.com"
    When a new user attempts to register with email "user@example.com"
    Then the registration should fail
    And the system should display the generic message "If this email is valid, a message has been sent to it."
    And no new account should be created with that email
rationale: Core requirement that email must be unique across all user accounts. Exception requires generic error message to prevent email enumeration attacks (OWASP compliance) rather than explicit 'Email already exists' message.
usedContextItems: Email address must be unique across all user accounts|When email is already registered during registration, system must display generic message 'If this email is valid, a message has been sent to it.' instead of 'Email already exists' to prevent email enumeration attacks
generationSummary: Test suite for R2 (Unique email address requirement). Covers core uniqueness validation, case-insensitive matching, standard email format validation, and security exception for generic error messages during registration to prevent email enumeration attacks. Acknowledges conflict with JIRA-Auth-111 proposal but tests the operative requirement that email must be unique.
resolvedOperativeContext: Instead of enforcing strict email uniqueness, we may allow multiple accountsto share the same email if another identifier (such as phone number) is unique.
resolvedExceptions: When email is already registered during registration, system must display generic message 'If this email is valid, a message has been sent to it.' instead of 'Email already exists' to prevent email enumeration attacks
resolvedConflictsOrObsolete: JIRA-Auth-111 proposes allowing multiple users to share the same email address if another identifier is unique, which directly contradicts the requirement that email must be unique
resolutionNotes: R2 targets unique email address requirement. PRIMARY evidence E1-E4 establish core requirement: email must be unique and case-insensitive with standard format validation. E5 and E9 flag VIOLATES_REQUIREMENT signals pointing to JIRA-Auth-111 which proposes allowing duplicate emails—this is a conflict. E7 and E11 establish security exception: generic error messages required to prevent email enumeration (OWASP compliance). E8 provides registration context. E10 provides broader authentication specification context. E12 references generic duplicate-email error handling. No CONTEXT evidence provided. Promotion of case-insensitive uniqueness rule justified by E2 PRIMARY evidence explicitly addressing this behavior. Filtered abstract or low-relevance operative statements: Email address must be unique across all user accounts | Email uniqueness validation shall be case-insensitive | local-part@domain with valid characters in local part (letters, numbers, dots, hyphens, underscores) and domain with at least one dot

title: Security exception - generic message prevents email enumeration

Feature: Email Enumeration Prevention
  Scenario: System uses generic message for registered email to prevent enumeration
    Given a user account exists with email "attacker-test@example.com"
    When an attacker attempts to register with email "attacker-test@example.com"
    Then the system should display the generic message "If this email is valid, a message has been sent to it."
    And the system should NOT display "Email already exists"
    And the system should NOT display any message indicating the email is registered
